$comment: languages-world-1 (10 November 2026): the WhatsApp allergen guard’s trigger words for VIETNAMESE (vi-VN): dị ứng, (không / bất) dung nạp, nhạy cảm, celiac, (sốc) phản vệ, không / không có / không cho / không chứa <allergen>, không ăn được, an toàn cho / với, phù hợp cho / với, có thể chứa, dấu vết, nhiễm chéo. Tone marks and diacritics fold away on both sides ("di ung" = "dị ứng"); đ is kept by the normaliser, so words with it are listed with d too (đậu phộng / dau phong). "không cá" is NOT a stem (it is inside "không cay"), nor bare "không có", nor bare "an toàn" (inside "hoàn toàn") or "phản vệ" ("phần về" folds to it). OPTION B, as every other language: absence / safety words only, NOT the bare allergen names (a presence question may reach the AI, which answers only from the tags and gets the caveat). Matched with the Unicode normaliser. caveatWords: a tagged label of the codex allergen set (stored in English, lower case) → the words a reply may use for it (matched on the raw lower-cased reply, so written as the AI writes them). The country has no allergen set of its own yet, so caveatWords are for 'codex' (as MX, SG, HK, MY, TH and AE).
